The expansion being performed was often incorrect, as it's possible for the tilde character to appear as part of the path where it should not be expanded to the user's home directory.

Properly supporting tilde expansion is complicated and requires additional study.  Instead of supporting it only partially, we have decided to simplify things and just drop tilde expansion for now.  See the discussion in issue #2619, as well as issues #2325 and #2555.
pr_comments: @kenkendk, you [previously mentioned](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/issues/2619#issuecomment-333094921) that `~` characters may be saved in the configuration and that an upgrade script may be needed.  Is this still a concern?

Yes, I think it is a potential problem. The source paths for the backup job is saved in the database. If we no longer expand them, we should run through all saved (source)paths and apply the expansion.

It could still be problematic for CLI users, but I expect them to be better at dealing with the issue.
For the build error, if you merge `master` into your branch, it should fix the build issue on Travis.

issue_context.title: Support native environment variable syntax
issue_context.body:
We might want to consider supporting the environment variable syntax of the user's operating system.  Currently, `Environment.ExpandEnvironmentVariables` only expands Windows-style variables (e.g., `%HOME%` is expanded but `$HOME` is not).

This continues the discussion from https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/pull/2836#discussion_r146110627:

> @warwickmm a day ago Contributor
This method is no longer necessary, as we can just call the built-in method. I decided to leave this refactoring for a separate pull request so that we don't pollute the diff in this pull request.
       @warwickmm
warwickmm 21 hours ago Contributor
Actually, it seems that ExpandEnvironmentVariables will only expand Windows-style environment variables (e.g., it will expand %HOME% but not $HOME). Do we need to better support Linux and MacOS here?
   @kenkendk
kenkendk 5 hours ago Owner
Yes, I have a comment about that in the code. Until now it has only used the Windows-style environment variable expansion (that is how .Net does) but it is simple to do the Linux style expansion as well.
>
> Should we just drop the old Windows-style environment variable expansion on non-Windows? I am not sure.... I think it may break something for current users expecting the expansion, but new users will be confused if it does not work as all the other stuff on their system....
      @warwickmm
warwickmm 26 minutes ago Contributor
I'm not sure what the best approach is. Is the main purpose here to expand environment variables specified in command-line options and filters? If so, one option is to only support (and document) the Windows-style syntax. Unless there's a way to support both on non-Windows environments if we want to avoid breaking current functionality?
>
> I'll create a separate issue regarding this matter so we can continue the discussion there.

Yes, I have a comment about that in the code. Until now it has only used the Windows-style environment variable expansion (that is how .Net does) but it is simple to do the Linux style expansion as well.

Should we just drop the old Windows-style environment variable expansion on non-Windows? I am not sure.... I think it may break something for current users expecting the expansion, but new users will be confused if it does not work as all the other stuff on their system....

I'm not sure what the best approach is.  Is the main purpose here to expand environment variables specified in command-line options and filters?  If so, one option is to only support (and document) the Windows-style syntax.  Unless there's a way to support both on non-Windows environments if we want to avoid breaking current functionality?

I'll create a separate issue regarding this matter so we can continue the discussion there.
